name: Network Engagement and Density Evidence

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether greater relevant local density creates more successful interactions and stronger retained use.
positioning.productLabel: Engagement-Effect Lens — based on Andrew Chen's public Cold Start materials
notAClaimOf: global user growth proving local utility

attribution.display: Based on Andrew Chen's public Cold Start materials

neutralParaphrase: Evaluate engagement at the atomic-network level: as relevant participants and connections become denser, do users complete more valuable interactions and retain better? Separate network-mediated improvement from product changes, promotions, seasonality, and blended global averages.

locator.value: Engagement, retention, marketplace metrics, and geographic concentration
Activation, cohort retention, and network-density diagnosis

requiredConditions: The atomic-network boundary and valuable interaction are defined.
Activity, successful interaction, and retained use can be distinguished.

requiredEvidence.description: Relevant active nodes and usable connections per atomic network over time.
Completed, relevant, timely, or mutually accepted interactions rather than raw messages, listings, or impressions.
Retention and frequency by local density, participant role, cohort, and maturation stage.
Product releases, promotions, seasonality, sales mix, and incentives that could explain engagement changes.

decisionQuestions: Which local density variable is plausibly connected to user value?
Does successful interaction improve as that density rises?
Do retention and frequency improve for both the hard and easy sides?
Do the effects persist after promotions, product changes, and cohort mix are controlled?
positiveSignals: Maturing atomic networks show more successful interactions and stronger cohort retention.
Time to value or failed-match rate improves with relevant density.
The hard side retains and continues contributing as demand grows.
The relationship holds across replicated networks rather than one blended aggregate.
redFlags: Management reports total users or messages without successful-interaction quality.
Global retention improves only because mature markets dominate the mix.
One participant side grows while the hard side churns or becomes overloaded.
Engagement rises only while incentives or notifications intensify.
disconfirmingEvidence: Retention is flat or worse in denser networks.
More participants increase congestion, spam, irrelevant supply, or search cost.
Interaction success is explained by a product release rather than density.
New atomic networks fail to reproduce the engagement relationship.
contraindications: Do not use global DAU or message volume as a density proxy.
Do not infer causal effect from a single cross-sectional correlation.
Do not aggregate participant roles whose incentives and retention differ.

instructions: Define the atomic-network denominator and successful interaction.
Segment cohorts by network maturity, density, and participant role.
Compare interaction success, frequency, and retention.
Test product, promotion, seasonality, and mix alternatives.
Conclude demonstrated, emerging, contradicted, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not calculate cohorts, density, or causal effect estimates.

sourceReliability.low: Management anecdotes or aggregate engagement only.
sourceReliability.medium: Cohort and network-unit data are available with partial reconciliation.
sourceReliability.high: Auditable event graphs, cohorts, role segmentation, and experiments converge.

evidenceStrength.low: Activity grows without demonstrated user value.
evidenceStrength.medium: Density and retention co-move but alternatives remain.
evidenceStrength.high: Repeated local evidence links density to successful interaction and durable retention.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Density, success, and retention covered for some networks.
evidenceCoverage.high: All participant roles, network stages, quality, cohorts, and alternatives covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: Some engagement depends on local participation.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Core retained value is materially density-dependent.

empiricalQualifications: Observational relationships may not identify causality.

rights.notes: Public doctrine is neutrally paraphrased; no book text is redistributed.

openIssues: Create network-archetype metric dictionaries and acceptable causal-test standards.
